subject: Grace period & conversion options for timebox - Apexlytics
messages:
From: Sarah Khan <sarah@apexlytics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-18T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Timebox wrap + short grace window?

Marcus — thanks for the continued support during our integration. The team finished the last set of ingestion tests this morning and we have a couple of asks before we close out the 4-week timebox: 1) can we get a short grace period after the timebox ends to validate live traffic and run A/B checks (two weeks would be ideal)? 2) what are our options to convert unused capacity into credits if we decide to scale, and how does that interact with any discounted committed pricing?

Attached is this morning's perf snapshot (apex-performance-report.pdf) — latency looks fine but we saw a spike when we enabled long context caching. If there's a playbook for a short hold-period we can use that too. Happy to hop on a quick call this week.

—Sarah
Head of ML Platform, Apexlytics
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Khan <sarah@apexlytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-19T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Timebox wrap + short grace window?

Sarah — appreciate the note and the perf snapshot. Congrats to your team on getting integration to this stage. Short answers up front: yes to a grace window, and we have two clean conversion paths you can pick from. Below is a concise set of options so you can pick what fits your procurement/ops cadence: 

Option A — 2-week grace period (no additional charge):
- Full read-only access to the same capacity as the timebox (same model, same throughput cap) for 14 days.
- If you convert to a committed monthly plan within 30 days after the grace window, we will apply a one-time onboarding credit equal to 15% of your total timebox consumption.
- If you do not convert, access will revert and billing stops; logs and artifacts persist for 90 days.

Option B — Convert unused capacity to prepaid credits + committed discount:
- We convert any remaining unconsumed token budget from the timebox into Redwood credits at a 1:1 token-equivalent rate.
- If you commit to a 3-month reserved package at sign-up, we can offer a 20% discount off the hosted per-token rate for the committed portion.
- Minimum commit in this path: 100k tokens/day (we can discuss lowering to 50k/day if needed).

Operational notes:
- We can enable a temporary traffic mirror hook during the grace window so you can validate live traffic without affecting production routing.
- We recommend keeping the long-context cache disabled until you validate the mirror; that was the spike source in your report.

I've attached a quick revision to the proposal (redwood-timebox-proposal-v3.pdf) that shows quantitative examples for both options. If you want, I can draft a mutual action plan to align dates and procurement steps.

–Marcus
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Sarah Khan <sarah@apexlytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-22T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Timebox wrap + short grace window?

Looping in Sales Ops to flag procurement details from our side: if Apexlytics prefers Option B and wants reserved capacity, procurement will need a PO or a signed SOW before we provision the committed pool. Standard terms: Net 30, one-time onboarding invoice for enterprise enablement (waivable in certain circumstances).

Action items for Apexlytics to speed conversion:
- Confirm which option (A or B) by EOD May 26.
- If Option B, confirm committed daily token minimum (100k or request for 50k).
- Legal: will need the approver name/email for the SOW/DocuSign send.

Aditya — can you confirm whether we can approve a reduced minimum (50k/day) for this account under the current promo bucket?

Thanks,
Laura
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Khan <sarah@apexlytics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Devon Lee <devon@apexlytics.com>
Date: 2026-05-25T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Timebox wrap + short grace window?

Thanks — that helps. Quick follow-ups after a sync with our finance and infra teams:
- We're leaning to Option B but the 100k/day minimum is higher than what our forecasts support. Can you provide a firm quote for lowering the committed minimum to 50k tokens/day and show the prorated discount impact?
- Alternatively, if you keep 100k/day minimum, would Redwood allow us a 2-week grace period + a refundable credit (applied toward the first month) equal to the difference between 50k and 100k daily for the first 30 days?

If you can sketch both numbers I can bring them to procurement tomorrow. We'd prefer minimal paperwork up front and to convert quickly if the numbers make sense.

—Sarah
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Khan <sarah@apexlytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Timebox wrap + short grace window?

Sarah — thanks for the clear framing. We can do a tailored path that minimizes paperwork while protecting both sides. Final proposal below (I'll also send this via DocuSign if you confirm):

Chosen approach (hybrid A/B):
- We grant a 14-day grace period immediately after your current timebox (no charge).
- During the grace window we will keep capacity capped at your current observed peak (we estimated ~70k tokens/day based on the attached report).
- If you sign a 3-month reserved commitment within 30 days after the grace window, we will:
  - Accept a lowered committed minimum of 50k tokens/day for the reserved portion.
  - Apply a one-time conversion credit equal to the difference between 100k/day and 50k/day for the first 30 days (this is the refundable credit you asked about) — effectively reducing your first invoice.
  - Provide a 10% volume discount on the committed portion (rather than the 20% headline), since this is a smaller minimum.

Why this structure: it gives Apexlytics two weeks to validate live traffic (no cost risk), removes a hard 100k/day barrier, and preserves predictable economics for both sides. If you prefer a pure Option B with 20% discount, we can do that but it would require the 100k/day minimum and standard PO/SOW pre-provisioning.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm acceptance of the hybrid approach by replying to this thread.
2) I'll generate a short SOW and send a DocuSign link (estimated signature-to-provision: 48 hours).
3) If you want the alternate 20%/100k plan, say so and we'll exchange the SOW version for that.

I've included links: DocuSign preview (https://www.docusign.com/overview/ABCDEF-APEX-1472) and the HubSpot record for visibility. I also attached the revised proposal that shows numeric examples (redwood-timebox-proposal-v3.pdf).

If you're good with this, I'll start the SOW and ask Legal to waive the onboarding fee.

–Marcus
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
